newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Wealthy farmers may face support limits - Fischler.
newsitem.headline: Wealthy farmers may face support limits - Fischler.

text.p: Wealthy farmers could lose some European Union farm subsidies under reforms being considered by the European Commission, Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler said on Monday.

The idea of concentrating resources on the most needy small family farms was "sacrificed on the altar of the 'level playing field'," during the EU's last reform of the common agriculture policy (CAP) in 1992, Fischler said in a speech prepared for a conference in Prague but made available in advance.

"The future of the CAP depends on a number of undeniable facts. We face a trend towards free agricultural trade, both within the WTO (World Trade Organisation) and the growing number of Free Trade Agreements that criss-cross the world," he said.

The future for Europe was to preserve a social-market economy in farming with a safety net made up of various forms of support with a greater dependence on environmental, structural and market policies.
"Now we can hear criticism in the rural communities and read in the press derogatory comments about some very wealthy people receiving huge set-aside payments and other premia."
This did not help create a positive image for farming in the EU and could make enemies at a time when friends were needed to improve the system, he told the conference.
"In this area, too, I will give careful consideration to all the arguments for and against," he said.
But he ruled out renationalisation of the CAP, which he said would have "catastrophic consequences".
The only direction for the CAP was, he said, "to develop the current policy from its 'new directions' to its logical conclusion."
Agricultural policy could not lead a life apart from consumer policy and environmental policy or concerns such as animal welfare. he added.
